predecessors.note: 'By fall 616, Du had settled in at Liuhe (六合, in modern Nanjing, Jiangsu)', fighting the Sui general Chen Leng; Du was born in Qi Province (near Jinan) and rebelled earlier (not on the page in months).

land.text: the infobox territory: 'Land south of the Huai River, roughly modern central and southern Jiangsu, Anhui, and parts of Zhejiang', drawn as a 130 km disc round Nanjing (Danyang, the later headquarters)

successors.note: 'In summer 620, Emperor Gaozu changed Du Fuwei's title to Prince of Wu, and bestowed on him the imperial surname of Li'; the infobox says he 'submitted to Tang around 619-620'. Du (as Li Fuwei) kept governing the land for the Tang until he was held at Chang'an in 622-623 and died on 20 April 624; Fu Gongshi rebelled in fall 623.

ledger.note: Fall 616: Du Fuwei settles at Liuhe. 'By fall 616, Du had settled in at Liuhe (六合, in modern Nanjing, Jiangsu).' The page gives the place, not a boundary; the later headquarters were Liyang and Danyang.

region.text: the infobox territory: 'Land south of the Huai River, roughly modern central and southern Jiangsu, Anhui, and parts of Zhejiang', drawn as a 130 km disc round Nanjing (Danyang, the later headquarters)

ledger.note: Summer 620: Du Fuwei becomes the Tang's Prince of Wu. 'In summer 620, Emperor Gaozu changed Du Fuwei's title to Prince of Wu, and bestowed on him the imperial surname of Li' (infobox 'Submitted to Tang around 619-620'). The land is Tang's through Du until 623-624; the tang-dynasty dossier should draw it as a vassal tint under counterpart du-fuwei-s-regime. Confidence 2: the submission year is a range.

wars.name: Du Fuwei against Chen Leng
wars.outcome: 'in spring 617, Du intentionally enraged Chen by sending Chen women clothes'; 'In fall 619, Li was sieging Chen at Jiangling, and Chen sought help from both Shen and Du'; Du submitted to Tang around 619-620.
wars.note: Chen Leng was the Sui general at Jiangdu; no place changed hands on the page. Du's rivals Shen Faxing and Li Zitong are separate dossiers.

certainty.note: A rebel warlord's land south of the Huai with no boundary; the infobox gives modern provinces only.

sources.title: Du Fuwei
sources.note: Infobox (territory, titles, base, submission 619-620, died 624), fall 616, spring 617, fall 619, summer 620.

notes: Rebel state Cliopatria lacks; slug du-fuwei-s-regime as ea-03-f suggested. One page; the Tang, Dou Jiande and Li Mi are not on it. Dates: the independent period 616-620 is 'fall 616' to 'summer 620'; the rebellion began earlier (Du was a rebel before 616) and as the Tang's Prince of Wu he governed until 622-623. The infobox gives Danyang and Liyang as headquarters without dates (capital years in identity are placeholders). The overlap with shen-faxing-s-liang and li-zitong-s-wu (all three drawn as soft discs round the lower Yangtze) is for the compiler to settle. The Tang dossier is not yet written.
